text:
Nora: Heads-up — saw a reproducible memory climb on staging yesterday during long-chat workloads after the batching heuristic tweak. Contexts > 8k tokens slowly grow KV layer RSS until OOM-ish. Repro steps and a tiny flame snippet below. :eyes:

Sam: ugh. which change? was it the merge-window heuristic from last week? can you drop the minimal repro?

Nora: repro is a 10-concurrent-chat loop hitting /v1/generate with long histories. command:```bash
VG_HEAPCHECK=1 ./bench_client --url http://staging:8080/generate --profiles longctx --concurrency 10 --iters 200
```flame: top frames are kv_page_alloc, kv_slot_reuse_free_path, cont_batch_merge_handler. pprof shows hot path in page reclamation waiting on head-of-line batch locks.

Lee: that stack rings bell — the batching merge path can hold a slot while merging batches which prevents page reclamation; with long contexts we keep pinning pages. two quick ideas: (1) short-term: disable merge coalescing (kv.merge_coalesce=false) to avoid long-held slots, (2) medium: make slot-release async so reclamation can proceed while merge continues.

Ana: hypothesis: split/merge logic creates many tiny fragments and reuse logic prefers exact-slot matches so we get fragmentation + delayed free. over time free pages count drops and we page-swap. can you dump ``kv.free_pages`` and ``kv.frag_ratio`` metrics from staging? I suspect frag_ratio >> 0.6 before crash. also the kernel selection tweak that reduced small-kernel mem copies may have changed access patterns and amplified fragmentation.

Nora: pulled metrics: kv.free_pages went from ~120k to 4k across the run, kv.frag_ratio climbed from 0.12 to 0.67. attaching a tiny trace: ```json
{"entries": [{"ts": 0, "free_pages": 120000, "frag": 0.12},{"ts": 90, "free_pages": 4000, "frag": 0.67}] }
```

infra-bot: CI perf-run #5234 (staging) finished: regression detected on mem-usage (+28% p50) for longctx profile. Full artifact: http://ci.internal/runs/5234/artifacts/kv-traces.tar.gz :warning:

Sam: ok let's triage: (A) flip kv.merge_coalesce=false on staging and run bench (B) add an opt-in async-slot-release patch and benchmark (C) add a short-term periodic kv.compact() every N requests for longctx to avoid page tailing. I can try (A) now.

Lee: also add a debug histogram for "slot-hold-ms" to see how long a slot stays pinned by the merge path. if head-of-line stalls are >50ms we get backpressure to allocator.

Ana: agree on metrics. I'll prototype async-release — should be small (handoff to a background reclaim worker). If we land that, fragmentation should reduce since frees won't be blocked by the merge lock.

Nora: thanks — Sam please post bench results. if (A) drops mem by even 10% we can hotfix. assign: @Sam to flip flag + run, @Ana to prototype async-release, @Lee to add slot-hold-ms metric. I'll keep reproducer and traces in the run artifact. :thumbsup:
